findings.passage: Requiring photo IDs for in-person voting is a solution in search of a problem. Instead, the real election problem is votes harvested illegally through absentee ballots, which this proposal fails to fix.
findings.note: Veto message from Governor Roy Cooper on Senate Bill 824, the act implementing the constitutional amendment requiring photographic identification to vote. The page is a scan of the signed message; the text was read from the image. It says photo ID for in-person voting addresses no real problem and points to absentee ballots as the real problem.

findings.passage: In addition, the proposed law puts up barriers to voting that will trap honest voters in confusion and discourage them with new rules, some of which haven't even been written yet.
findings.note: Same veto message on SB 824. Says the law's new rules would confuse and discourage honest voters, and that some rules were not yet written.

findings.passage: Finally, the fundamental flaw in the bill is its sinister and cynical origins: It was designed to suppress the rights of minority, poor and elderly voters. The cost of disenfranchising those voters or any citizens is too high, and the risk of taking away the fundamental right to vote is too great, for this law to take effect.
findings.note: Same veto message on SB 824. States his reasons about the bill's purpose and its cost to voters' rights, ending with 'Therefore, I veto the bill.'
subjects: effect on minority, poor and elderly voters

findings.motion: Governor's veto of Senate Bill 824, Implementation of Voter ID Const. Amendment
findings.note: Governor vetoed the bill carrying out the voter photo ID constitutional amendment. The Senate overrode the veto 33-12 on 2018-12-18, and the House override motion passed 68-43 on 2018-12-19 (veto-override roll calls shown on the same page).

findings.passage: "Requiring photo IDs for in-person voting is a solution in search of a problem," Cooper wrote. "Instead, the real election problem is votes harvested illegally through absentee ballots, which this proposal fails to fix."
findings.note: ABC11 (WTVD) quotes the governor's written veto explanation for SB 824, the bill putting the voter photo ID amendment into law. He says in-person photo ID is not needed and points to absentee ballots as the real problem.
subjects: mail and absentee ballot fraud and ID
